speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me determine the cause, can you describe what the spinning sensation feels like and how long each episode lasts? Additionally, have you noticed any associated symptoms like hearing loss, tinnitus, or difficulty walking?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; your age and the position-dependent nature of the spinning sensation strongly suggest a benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). To confirm this, I will need to see the results of a Dix-Hallpike maneuver. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike_Maneuver. Are you currently taking any medications, especially for blood pressure or cholesterol?
